propositions: Blocking LINK events written before structural comparability can cause an epic to be blocked by its own child or create incorrect cousin edges that distort ready/next-batch calculations and parent-first cascade

A store-wide scan must classify blocking edges as ancestor-blocking (endpoint is ancestor of other), mis-escalated (resolver returns different pair), or unreadable (endpoint cannot be reduced) by re-resolving against the current rule, reusing the reducer's compiled deps[] rather than replaying LINK/UNLINK

Repair must write replacement links before removing stale ones to ensure that an interruption leaves a superset converging on the next run rather than losing a dependency, and must decline pairs whose unlink would cancel a different relation (ambiguous-pair)

Read-only doctor scans must not trigger store reconvergence (init_only=True), while --repair runs must support reconvergence; repair must refuse to run while a reconciler pass is in flight and must force-write a pre-doctor-repair tag at the pre-run OID as a rollback anchor

The command must not hold the tracker write lock across multiple event writes, as the non-reentrant lock causes each inner write to timeout waiting for an outer acquire held by the repair process itself

Mis-escalated edges whose resolved source ticket is closed cannot be repaired (add_dependency forbids links with closed source), but these are inert because closed tickets never appear in ready/next-batch, so they do not affect scheduling
